decks.name: LeetCode #621 - Task Scheduler
decks.description: Schedule tasks with cooldown period to minimize total time

cards.question: Task Scheduler: Given a characters array tasks, representing the tasks a CPU needs to do, where each letter represents a different task. Tasks could be done in any order. Each task is done in one unit of time. For each unit of time, the CPU could complete either one task or just be idle. However, there is a non-negative integer n that represents the cooldown period between two same tasks (the same letter in the array), that is that there must be at least n units of time between any two same tasks. Return the least number of units of times that the CPU will take to finish all the given tasks.

solutions.name: Brute Force
solutions.explanation: Simulate entire scheduling process. Count frequency of each task, maintain list of task counts. For each time unit, check last n processed tasks to find which tasks are available (not in cooldown), select task with highest count that can run, decrement count, track in processed list. Continue until all tasks done. O(t*n) time where t is total time units needed, checking last n elements each iteration. O(t) space to store processed tasks.

solutions.name: Max-Heap
solutions.explanation: Use max-heap to prioritize most frequent tasks with queue for cooldown tracking. Count task frequencies, negate for max-heap. Each time unit: if heap empty jump to next task ready time, else pop most frequent task, decrement count, add to cooldown queue with ready time. Move tasks from queue back to heap when ready. O(m) time processing m tasks, O(1) space for at most 26 tasks. Efficient simulation approach.

solutions.name: Greedy
solutions.explanation: Calculate minimum idle time based on most frequent task. Sort task counts, most frequent task determines minimum structure. Calculate idle slots as (maxFreq - 1) * n. Fill idle slots with other tasks, each contributing min(maxFreq - 1, count). Remaining idle time plus total tasks gives answer. O(m) time for counting and O(1) sort of 26 elements. O(1) space. Mathematical approach avoiding simulation.

O(1) space for fixed array. Most elegant solution deriving answer mathematically.
